title: Basic user-id as identity beside an encoded credential
summary: A synthetic log line that records the user-id in cleartext next to the Authorization header whose encoded token carries the same user-id and the password.
rationale: The password is the confidential portion; the user-id identifies the user but the scheme does not say whether it is public. Credential scope and personal-data scope are different populations, so the cleartext user-id must not be folded into the credential span and its own status stays open. The encoded token is the credential span.

expectation.rationale: Project policy, maintainer-only (ADR 0020, ADR 0019 item 7 (#114), user-id): expect it to be flagged. The encoded token is the secret span (it carries the password); the cleartext user-id is a companion span, not secret, and no personal-data expectation is stated: credential and personal-data populations stay separate. Finalized by the sole maintainer alone: not reviewed, not independent validation, queued for retro-review (#154). The question, options, strongest dissent and reversing evidence are in the review history.

sources.supports: the exchange of those credentials will have the effect of identifying that user even if the content within credentials remains confidential

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Maintainer-only (ADR 0020): decided by the sole maintainer, not reviewed, not independent validation; queued for retro-review (#154). Authored from the cited standards read on 2026-10-03, before any scanner was consulted. All values are synthetic and were not tested against any service. Header coalescing, parser and action policy, decoded-token mapping and product masking stay with the downstream repositories.
